title: Adaptive prefix reuse + slab coalescing for cross-request KV deduplication
creator: Diego Chen
description:
Problem: High tail memory pressure and redundant KV fragments across concurrent requests cause increased GPU memory usage and decreased effective batch sizes. Current exact-prefix fingerprinting is precise but brittle for lightly-mutated prompts and wastes memory storing near-duplicate KV slices.

Proposal: Implement an adaptive prefix-reuse engine that uses a two-tier dedupe strategy: (1) cheap, approximate similarity hashing (LSH + short-segment signatures) to identify high-probability near-duplicates across requests; (2) high-confidence validation and coalescing into contiguous GPU memory slabs for reuse. Combine this with a slab coalescing allocator that groups short KV fragments into shared memory pools (slabs) per-model-and-sequence-class to reduce small-allocation fragmentation on CUDA devices. Introduce an async rehousing step to safely remap live KV references to coalesced slabs without blocking inference paths. Add per-tenant soft quotas to influence eviction decisions and preserve fairness.
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Proof-of-concept LSH-based short-segment signature generator and approximate cross-request index (in-memory bloom+LSH table).
Phase 2: Slab allocator prototype on CPU then port to CUDA using cuMemPool / custom allocator, with instrumentation hooks for allocation/eviction stats.
Phase 3: Safe async rehousing: copy, validate checksum, swap pointer atomically, update refcounts; provide fallback to original KV if validation fails.
Phase 4: Integrate with scheduler: expose hints to continuous-batching layer so similar requests land in same micro-batches when possible.
Phase 5: Gradual rollout: runtime flag gating, canary across 5% of traffic then 25% with telemetry checks, finally 100% if no regressions.
milestones: Wide rollout and perf regression sweep - 2026-03-31
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end canary demonstrates >=15% reduction in GPU memory consumed for mixed prompt workload compared to baseline
No more than 3% increase in token-generation p50 and <8% increase in p99 during canary window, otherwise roll back
No correctness regressions in rehomed KV slices (checksum validation and deterministic outputs on 1000 synthetic prompts)
Telemetry shows a net decrease in small-allocation count and fragmentation metrics on affected devices
performance_targets: Target: 20% reduction in peak GPU memory for workloads with many short prompt prefixes
Target: 8% improvement in effective throughput (tokens/sec) under the same hardware budget
Fallback: if slab coalescing introduces >10% p99 latency regression, disable coalescing on that model variant
risks: Approximate dedupe can yield false positives that cause incorrect reuse of incompatible KV fragments; mitigate with strong validation and short TTLs for approximate matches
Async rehousing complexity may introduce pointer-swap race conditions on CUDA; requires careful ordering and atomic updates with fallbacks
Per-tenant quotas and fairness heuristics can increase eviction churn if thresholds mis-set; needs live tuning and dashboards
Driver-level memory API availability varies across cloud GPUs which may complicate portable allocator implementation

comments: 2026-02-21 - Diego Chen: Initial ticket created after spike showed 18% fragmentation on short prompt tails. PoC preferred LSH over SHA1 fingerprinting for tolerance to small edits.

2026-02-26 - Ava Thompson: Implemented LSH PoC and small benchmark harness. Early results: approximate index finds 72% of near-duplicates with 1% false-positive rate on synthetic edits. Moving to slab allocator design.
2026-03-03 - PM feedback (Lydia Park): Ensure per-tenant isolation — add soft quotas and metrics to avoid noisy-host impact on single-tenant latency.
2026-03-05 - Security review (notes): No customer plaintext is stored in index; only hashed signatures and short metadata. Recommend threat modeling for pointer-swap attack surface.

2026-03-08 - Engineering review (Kai Müller): CUDA allocator approach looks good; flagged device portability. Action: add fallback allocator that uses existing CUDA allocation path on unsupported devices.
2026-03-10 - Ava Thompson: Merged CPU slab prototype to feature branch; next is CUDA port. Created canary dashboard and instrumentation for allocation churn, WrongReuseCounter, and rehousing latency.
